title: Language Access in Neurology Care
summary: Build safer multilingual neurology workflows for stroke timelines, seizure histories, cognitive testing, consent, medications, and follow-up.
body_markdown:
###


Begin interpretation when the stroke pathway is activated, in parallel with stabilization and assessment. Confirm the source of each time point, last known baseline, medication names, and critical numbers without delaying emergency care.


###


Keep the witness and patient accounts separate. Record sequence, laterality, responsiveness, duration, recovery, source, and absolute times when available. Read back medication names, doses, and time estimates that may affect care.


###


Interpretation does not make a test version valid or preserve its original norms. Use a validated language version and follow its manual. If a suitable version is unavailable, document the limitation and avoid overstating the score.


###


Family members can provide valuable observations and support, but they should not automatically replace an approved interpretation pathway. Keep their clinical account separate and attributed, and follow patient preference and organizational policy.


###


Confirm the diagnosis or working explanation, medication names and dose changes, titration dates, warning signs, activity guidance, appointments, tests, and callback route. Use teach-back through the interpreter and provide written instructions that match the plan.
